title: The pupil who never forgot

data.source: Recorded numbers read from the Phoenix files named below (SEC11b itself used 12 real OpenML data sets and was not re-run: it needs the network). The toy is this room's own: 1200 seeded sets of five lessons.
data.licence: none needed for the toy (generated here from a seed)

prediction: Phoenix registered that the CRR-inspired rule SEC would be within 0.01 of a costly tuning sweep on at least 0.80 of fresh units. In this room's toy, a pass mark of "not behind the tuned learner" lets through a learner frozen after lesson one whenever the lessons are nearly alike, and stops it when they differ.
baseline: A full tuning sweep, a constant carried over from earlier work, no protection at all, and a learner frozen after its first task. The frozen learner is the one that matters: a pass it can reach says nothing.
why: Phoenix's registered test printed FAIL: 0.792 against 0.80. The older passes are uninformative because a frozen learner could reach them, and the toy shows how. The CRR-specific hopes for continual learning failed in their tested forms. SEC stays an engineering candidate.
phoenix_status: P09-SEC11b: "Verdict as printed by the frozen claim-specific scorer: FAIL" (H1 0.792 against 0.80); P09-SEC11 closed VOID; SEC6R "PASS-0 UNINFORMATIVE", "no PASS-2"; method graded KNOWN; specificity S2, novelty N0, "no finding". CL1: FLAME, synthetic, "no PASS claimable". "Phoenix may not describe it as a validated CRR law."
